programme: No single recognisable module. The concordant set splits into unrelated families: three nuclear hormone receptors (NR5A2, THRA, RARG) that converge on ESR1/RARA/RARB and retinoid-thyroid-controlled differentiation genes; a Notch/CSL pathway member (RBPJ, with HES1, NOTCH1, NOTCH3, FOXP3 among its targets); a pluripotency factor (NANOG); a circadian/hypoxia-response bHLH (BHLHE40, wired to CLOCK/BMAL1/PER1/PER2/CRY1); a CCR4-NOT deadenylase subunit (CNOT7); and a handful of largely independent developmental or immediate-early factors (SIX4, FOXP4, EGR4, KDM5D) plus ZNF165, which is explicitly flagged discordant and should not be read as agreeing evidence at all. None of these share a defined complex, a common target set, or a documented pathway link to one another.
role_in_a: Individually, several factors have direct breast-cancer literature: NR5A2/LRH1 sustains ESR1 signalling and endocrine resistance (PMID 40544998), SIX4 and RARG are named breast-cancer therapeutic targets (PMID 37905439, 41721968), RBPJ/Notch drives TNBC chemoresistance (PMID 41933509), NANOG marks breast cancer stem-like cells (PMID 41793693, 42624838), and BHLHE40 mediates hypoxic radioresistance (PMID 42505118, 41613788). These are separate, factor-specific roles, not one shared programme.
role_in_b: Almost nothing is placed in Sjögren's Syndrome directly: Open Targets shows no association for THRA, RARG, RBPJ, NANOG, FOXP4, ZNF165, CNOT7, EGR4, SIX4, and only very low or middling percentiles for NR5A2 and KDM5D. The only two retrieved hits are tangential — a Bhlhe40/Th17 autoimmune paper that does not name Sjögren's specifically (PMID 41087718), and a salivary-gland acinar culture paper that uses NANOG as a stemness marker rather than studying Sjögren's pathogenesis (PMID 25416669).
shared_axis: There is no mechanism in the retrieved material that ties these factors together as a module operating in both tissues; any shared story would have to be built by picking one factor (e.g. BHLHE40's Th17 link) and ignoring the other eleven.
reasoning: Twelve concordant factors spanning nuclear receptors, Notch signalling, a deadenylase complex, a pluripotency factor and several unrelated developmental genes do not add up to one nameable programme, and the record places almost all of them in breast cancer alone with no Sjögren's evidence beyond two thin, non-specific papers. Per the task's own caution, a pair this heterogeneous with this little disease-B evidence should not be forced into a story.
support: PMID 40544998 (NR5A2/LRH1 sustains ESR1 signalling, endocrine resistance, breast cancer only); PMID 37905439 (SIX4 as ER+ breast cancer target, breast cancer only); PMID 41133246 (FOXP4 in breast cancer bone metastasis, breast cancer only); PMID 42505118 and 41613788 (BHLHE40 in breast cancer hypoxia/radioresistance); PMID 41087718 (Bhlhe40-mediated Th17 response in unspecified autoimmune disease, not confirmed as Sjögren's); PMID 41933509 (RBPJ/Notch in TNBC chemosensitivity, breast cancer only); PMID 41793693 and 42624838 (NANOG in breast cancer stemness); PMID 25416669 (NANOG used as marker in salivary gland acinar culture work referencing Sjögren's, not a pathogenic role); PMID 41721968 (RARG in solid tumour progression, breast cancer only); PMID 40806280 (CNOT7 in breast cancer); PMID 35326716 (EGR4 in HER+ breast cancer); PMID 39865831 (ZNF165 as pan-cancer biomarker, breast cancer only, and this factor is flagged discordant). None of these connect the two diseases jointly.
how_to_falsify: Take the strongest candidate axis — NR5A2, THRA and RARG as a nuclear-receptor module — and test by ChIP-seq/co-IP whether they co-occupy shared enhancers or physically complex together in both breast tumour tissue and Sjögren's-affected salivary/lacrimal gland or PBMC samples; if they show coordinated, tissue-matched co-binding in both diseases, a real shared module exists and this incoherent verdict is wrong. Absence of such co-binding would confirm the account.
caveats: 273 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the comparison count reflects correlated subgroups rather than 273 independent replications. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed STAT1, IRF1, CIITA, SPI1, FLI1, DNMT1, TCF4, NCOA1 — the classic blood/immune and antigen-presentation transcription factors — so the immune-coherent story a blood-tissue pairing would normally suggest was stripped out before ranking; that is the likely reason the remaining factors look disjointed, not an oversight. ZNF165 is marked discordant despite its recurrence count and should not be treated as agreeing evidence. The single-view exclusions (TRIB3, SALL1, RERE, MYB, NCOR2, SMARCD3, HDAC9, MSX1, NR4A2, SMAD4, HOXB9, ZNF304) rule out any account built on one subgroup's top hit.
